scenes.title: 1975 Sunny Arizona State Walkway: '2 Years Unpaid (0% Yes!)' Retreating Immediately to '2-Hour Zoo Trip (50% Yes — 3x Jump!)'
scenes.era: 1975, Palm-lined sunlit campus walkway, Arizona State University, Tempe

layout.description: Sunlit high-key 1975 Arizona university quad walkway with warm brick paving, bright desert daylight, and a clipboard researcher comparing two crisp signup sheets — **Direct Zoo Ask Alone: 16.7% YES** versus **2-Year Ask ('NO!') -> Retreat to 2-Hour Zoo Trip: 50.0% YES (3x!)**.

positions.who: Robert Cialdini / Campus Researcher mannequin (in 1975 collared polo/button-down shirt and chinos holding County Youth clipboard)
positions.where: taking half a polite step back with an understanding palm gesture as he flips the top '2-Year Weekly Counselor' sheet over to reveal the smaller 'One 2-Hour Zoo Chaperone' sheet!

positions.who: Campus Student Walker mannequin (in 1975 denim jacket/collared shirt carrying textbooks)
positions.where: first shaking head firmly 'No way!' at the 2-year request — then relaxing, nodding warmly, and signing the 2-hour Saturday zoo clipboard!

props.name: flip-over two-stage Clipboard ('Request 1: 2 Years Weekly [0% Yes]' -> 'Concession 2: One 2-Hour Zoo Trip [50% Yes!]')
props.period_detail: shows the immediate Big-No -> Small-Yes pivot in one physical prop

props.name: 3-Condition Comparison Stand ('Direct Ask: 16.7% | Two Different Requesters: 10.7% | Same-Person Concession: 50–55.5%!')
props.period_detail: visualizes both the 3x jump and Experiment 2's reciprocity proof

actions.verb_sequence: presents the 2-Year Weekly sheet -> Student Walker shakes head 'No' -> Researcher nods understandingly and flips down to the 2-Hour Zoo sheet -> Student Walker smiles and signs name cleanly

reactions.reaction: walks away feeling satisfied at reaching a fair two-hour compromise
tallies 50% compliance — triple the direct-ask group

scenes.wardrobe: 1975 American Southwest campus attire: wide-collar cotton shirts, corduroy/denim jacket, flared chinos, canvas sneakers.
scenes.lighting: Bright high-key sunny Tempe campus daylight.
scenes.recognition_hook: Ask strangers straight up to chaperone a two-hour zoo trip and 83% walk past — get rejected on a two-year job ten seconds first, and half of them say yes!

key_visual.description: a sunlit 1975 university walkway where a clipboard researcher flips from a rejected '2-Year Counselor' sheet to a '2-Hour Zoo Trip' sheet as a textbook-carrying student signs beside a 16.7%-to-50% chart

scenes.title: Experiment 2's Genius Control: Why Switching Requesters Crashed to 10.7%!

layout.description: Same sunlit quad where Requester A walks away after 'No' and Requester B steps up asking for the 2-hour zoo trip.

positions.where: splitting the big ask and small ask across two separate strangers — watching compliance plunge to 10.7%!
declining Requester B easily because B made zero personal concession

props.name: Two-Requester 10.7% vs Same-Requester 55.5% placard
props.period_detail: proves Reciprocal Concessions (not mere contrast) powers the effect

actions.verb_sequence: gets 'No' on 2 years and leaves -> Requester B asks for 2 hours -> Walker declines politely

reactions.reaction: confirms Gouldner's Reciprocity Norm is the causal engine

scenes.recognition_hook: Split the 2-year ask and 2-hour ask across two DIFFERENT people, and the magic vanishes (10.7%) — proving you were repaying a personal concession!

scenes.title: 1976 Civic Donor-Drive Proof: 84% Actually Showed Up!

layout.description: Bright welcoming campus donation check-in table where pledged Door-in-the-Face donors arrive right on schedule.

positions.where: checking in at 84% real behavioral show-up rate AND volunteering phone numbers for future drives

props.name: 84% Real Show-Up & Future Volunteering ledger
props.period_detail: proves reciprocal concessions build genuine internal ownership rather than hollow talk

actions.verb_sequence: checks in cheerfully and signs future volunteer roster

scenes.recognition_hook: Because people feel THEY steered the compromise, 84% actually showed up on donation day!

scenes.title: The Consumer Shield: Judging Offer #2 Without Anchor #1

layout.description: Sunlit desk where a buyer covers up a giant crossed-out 'Enterprise $999' box with their hand to evaluate the '$199 Standard' tier cleanly on its own merits.

positions.where: physically covering the decoy mega-tier and asking 'Is $199 worth it to me standalone?'

props.name: pricing sheet with covered Decoy Tier #1

actions.verb_sequence: places palm over giant Tier #1 -> evaluates Tier #2 calmly against real budget

scenes.recognition_hook: Whenever a salesperson sighs and retreats from an overpriced package to a 'special compromise,' cover Offer #1 with your hand before deciding!
